en: Āsavasāsavadukādi, Kusalattika (The Triplet of the Wholesome, beginning with the dyads of the taints and that which is subject to taints).

Dependent on a wholesome state that is both with taints (*sāsava*) and not a taint itself (*no āsava*), there arises a state that is neither a taint nor not a taint and is not wholesome, by way of root condition (*hetupaccaya*). Under root [condition], one; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, one.

Dependent on an unwholesome state that is both a taint and with taints, there arises a state that is neither a taint nor not a taint and is not unwholesome, by way of root condition. ... Under root [condition], three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, three.

Conditioned by a state that is both with taints and not a taint, and indeterminate, there arises a state that is neither without taints nor a taint, nor indeterminate, by way of root condition... Three for root; ... [and so on] ... three for non-disappearance.
(The "Twin-Duad of Taints and States Associated with Taints" is similar to the "Duad of Taints and States with Taints.")
